Potražni timovi pretraživali su područje oko sela, smještenih unutar 10 kilometara (6 milja) od Chiboka, od kasne nedjelje do ponedjeljka, tražeći dodatne žrtve. Stanovnici su izvijestili da su naoružani ljudi progonili i ubijali mještane koji su bježali. Barnabas Tanko, član lokalne obrambene skupine u Kwadi, izjavio je da su napadači naišli na otpor u Kautikariju, što je rezultiralo smrću šestorice od njih. Stanovnici su pripisali velik broj smrtnih slučajeva i rašireno uništenje domova sporoj vojnoj reakciji. Tvrde da su napadači imali pet sati da siju uništenje prije nego što je konačno stigao vojni zrakoplov. Tanko je izvijestio da su napadi započeli oko 8 sati ujutro po lokalnom vremenu i trajali do 13 sati bez ikakve vojne intervencije. Također je izjavio da su se, ugledavši borbeni zrakoplov, napadači povukli u grmlje. Glasnogovornik nigerijske vlade izjavio je da su vojska i zrakoplovstvo raspoređeni na to područje, ali su stigli 'malo prekasno'. Stanovnici su osporili tu tvrdnju, nazvavši je neistinitom.

article_content: Fernando Alonso outperformed championship contenders Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton by setting the fastest lap in the first practice session of the Singapore Grand Prix. Alonso mastered the challenging Marina Bay street circuit, clocking a time of 1 minute, 49.056 seconds. Hamilton was a tenth of a second behind, while Rosberg was only two hundredths of a second slower than his Mercedes teammate and title rival. The Red Bull drivers, Sebastian Vettel and Daniel Ricciardo, finished fourth and fifth respectively. However, Vettel encountered an engine issue late in the session and had to stop on the track. Nico Rosberg experienced a loose wing mirror, which he removed while driving. Lewis Hamilton trails Rosberg by 22 points in the championship standings. Kimi Raikkonen, Alonso's teammate, achieved a competitive seventh place. Jean-Eric Vergne of Toro Rosso delivered a strong performance until an electronics malfunction briefly blocked the pit exit. Jenson Button also faced technical problems that limited his track time, finishing eighth. Daniil Kvyat of Toro Rosso and Sergio Perez of Force India rounded out the top ten. The Williams cars showed surprisingly poor pace. Despite expectations that the twisty circuit would challenge the team after their success at the high-speed Belgian and Italian races, Felipe Massa finished 13th and Valtteri Bottas 15th. Vettel, plagued by reliability issues this season, stopped near the pit lane exit due to an engine problem. Red Bull team principal Christian Horner indicated that Vettel might struggle to participate in the second session. Horner stated the engine change would take about three and a half hours, significantly reducing Vettel's track time. The session marked the debut of new restrictions on pit-car radio transmissions. While the FIA delayed a ban on broader radio messages about car performance until 2015, they retained the ban on driver coaching. Rosberg and Hamilton were heard inquiring about competitors' tyres and performance, prompting curt responses from their teams. The 90-minute session was largely uneventful, with most drivers familiar with the circuit's demanding layout. Hamilton appeared relaxed, following his victory at the Italian Grand Prix.

article_content: Journalism and national security have weathered decades of deception; both can withstand a degree of unexpected truth. Disclosing government secrets and classified documents to adversaries, or even allies, is undoubtedly illegal; historically, it has been termed espionage. The current discourse has shifted, with proponents of disseminating stolen documents to the broader digital realm advocating for transparency. Conversely, opponents of WikiLeaks' release of diplomatic cables on Sunday denounce it as an act of terrorism warranting comprehensive government sanctions. A measured perspective acknowledges the potential harm and risks to national security in publishing a quarter-million State Department documents online. Yet, from a citizen's standpoint, it is profoundly satisfying to learn the true sentiments of government leaders, contrasting with official pronouncements, releases, and communiqués often presented as factual government information. It is refreshing to learn that Saudi leaders, despite projecting regional solidarity, harbor concerns about Iran. I also value knowing that the DEA is aware of an Afghan vice president's visit to the UAE carrying $52 million in cash. Even if I am discomfited by the suggestion that our diplomats are being pressured by other nations to accept Guantanamo Bay detainees, I prefer knowing the truth over contrived explanations. The primary danger, in my view, lies not in revealing classified material but in our tendency to overreact, whether to genuine security threats like the shoe and underwear bombers, or, in this instance, to a massive data dump. Our heightened reactivity to security concerns, coupled with an increasing indifference to threats against our own civil liberties, might lead us, in the wake of the WikiLeaks release, to permit government agencies to infringe upon the universal accessibility of the Internet or to create exceptions to First Amendment freedoms. While official disapproval may target WikiLeaks and its founder, there is also palpable resentment directed toward the media for providing a structured outlet for these documents. Without print media, the information would be presented haphazardly, making it difficult to analyze or verify its authenticity. Since WikiLeaks' earlier releases of low-level Defense Department documents pertaining to the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, I have yet to encounter anyone who has thoroughly examined even a small fraction of the leaked documents. While some argue that the digital age has supplanted traditional journalism, the work of journalists at The New York Times, The Guardian, Der Spiegel, and El Pais demonstrates that they are still actively involved in sifting through information, confirming its accuracy, editing, and presenting it to the public. Over several weeks, these publications have also collaborated with their governments and with WikiLeaks to vet the material and redact information that could pose a clear threat to individuals in other countries. We all recognize the illegality of disclosing state secrets, even those classified without valid justification. We also acknowledge that governments have historically misled the American public in the name of national security, whether regarding war preparations or dealings with allies and adversaries. Journalists find solace in the adage that sunlight is the best disinfectant, a sentiment echoed by Abraham Lincoln: 'Let the people know the facts and the country will be safe.' I acknowledge the risks associated with these illegally obtained insights into government discussions and deliberations, but we must not allow this to be used as a pretext to attack a free press or to increase government secrecy. During a discussion with my journalism class on the WikiLeaks controversy, my graduate students identified potential dangers in both overreactions: curtailing our constitutional freedoms and the government becoming even more deceitful. That would constitute a genuine transgression. The opinions expressed in this commentary are solely those of Timothy McNulty.
translated_content: Novinarstvo i nacionalna sigurnost preživjeli su desetljeća obmana; oboje mogu izdržati i određenu dozu neočekivane istine. Otkrivanje državnih tajni i povjerljivih dokumenata neprijateljima, ili čak saveznicima, nedvojbeno je nezakonito; povijesno gledano, to se nazivalo špijunažom. Trenutni diskurs se promijenio, pri čemu zagovornici širenja ukradenih dokumenata u širem digitalnom prostoru zagovaraju transparentnost. S druge strane, protivnici WikiLeaksovog objavljivanja diplomatskih depeša u nedjelju osuđuju to kao čin terorizma koji zaslužuje sveobuhvatne državne sankcije. Odvažna perspektiva prepoznaje potencijalnu štetu i rizike za nacionalnu sigurnost u objavljivanju četvrt milijuna dokumenata State Departmenta na internetu. Ipak, iz perspektive građanina, iznimno je zadovoljavajuće saznati prave osjećaje državnih čelnika, u suprotnosti sa službenim izjavama, priopćenjima i komunikéima koji se često predstavljaju kao činjenične državne informacije. Osvježavajuće je saznati da saudijski čelnici, unatoč projiciranju regionalne solidarnosti, gaje zabrinutost zbog Irana. Također cijenim što DEA zna za posjet afganistanskog potpredsjednika UAE-u prošle godine s 52 milijuna dolara u gotovini. Čak i ako me uznemiruje sugestija da druge nacije vrše pritisak na naše diplomate da prihvate zatočenike iz zaljeva Guantanamo, draže mi je znati istinu nego izmišljena objašnjenja. Po mom mišljenju, glavna opasnost ne leži u otkrivanju povjerljivog materijala, već u našoj sklonosti pretjeranoj reakciji, bilo na stvarne sigurnosne prijetnje poput bombaša cipela i bombaša samoubojice, ili, u ovom slučaju, na masovno ispuštanje podataka. Naša pojačana reaktivnost na sigurnosne brige, zajedno sa sve većom ravnodušnošću prema prijetnjama našim vlastitim građanskim slobodama, mogla bi nas navesti, nakon objave WikiLeaksa, da dopustimo državnim agencijama da naruše univerzalnu dostupnost interneta ili da stvore iznimke od sloboda Prvog amandmana. Iako službeno neodobravanje može biti usmjereno na WikiLeaks i njegovog osnivača, također postoji opipljiv ogorčenost usmjerena prema medijima zbog pružanja strukturiranog izlaza za ove dokumente. Bez tiskanih medija, informacije bi bile predstavljene nasumično, što bi otežalo analizu ili provjeru njihove autentičnosti. Budući da nitko koga sam sreo nije temeljito pregledao čak ni mali dio procurjelih dokumenata nakon ranijih objava WikiLeaksa dokumenata Ministarstva obrane niže razine koji se odnose na ratove u Afganistanu i Iraku. Iako neki tvrde da je digitalno doba zamijenilo tradicionalno novinarstvo, rad novinara u The New York Timesu, The Guardianu, Der Spiegelu i El Paisu pokazuje da su oni još uvijek aktivno uključeni u prosijavanje informacija, potvrđivanje njihove točnosti, uređivanje i predstavljanje javnosti. Tijekom nekoliko tjedana, ove su publikacije također surađivale sa svojim vladama i s WikiLeaksom kako bi provjerile materijal i redigirale informacije koje bi mogle predstavljati jasnu prijetnju pojedincima u drugim zemljama. Svi smo svjesni nezakonitosti otkrivanja državnih tajni, čak i onih klasificiranih bez valjanog opravdanja. Također priznajemo da su vlade povijesno obmanjivale američku javnost u ime nacionalne sigurnosti, bilo da se radi o pripremama za rat ili odnosima sa saveznicima i protivnicima. Novinari pronalaze utjehu u izreci da je sunčeva svjetlost najbolje dezinfekcijsko sredstvo, što je potvrdio i Abraham Lincoln: 'Neka ljudi znaju činjenice i zemlja će biti sigurna.' Priznajem rizike povezane s tim ilegalno stečenim uvidima u vladine rasprave i promišljanja, ali ne smijemo dopustiti da se to iskoristi kao izgovor za napad na slobodni tisak ili za povećanje državne tajnovitosti. Tijekom rasprave sa svojim razredom novinarstva o kontroverzi WikiLeaksa, moji studenti diplomskog studija prepoznali su potencijalne opasnosti u obje pretjerane reakcije: smanjenje naših ustavnih sloboda i da vlada postane još više varljiva. To bi predstavljalo pravu povredu. Mišljenja iznesena u ovom komentaru isključivo su mišljenja Timothyja McNultyja.

article_content: By Hugo Duncan. Former Canadian Bank of England Governor Mark Carney is pictured with the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, Danny Alexander, at a previous event. For the Bank of England’s annual summer party, Governor Mark Carney decided the event needed to be more inclusive. However, for many staff members, the Canadian governor’s decision to alter the tradition just wasn’t cricket. The Bank’s first foreign governor has arranged a rounders match to replace cricket because he believes the summer game to be too exclusive. Other activities at the event in Roehampton, South West London, taking place tomorrow, include five-a-side football, tennis, a three-legged race, an egg-and-spoon race, tug-of-war, and welly throwing. Mr. Carney stopped short of introducing ice hockey, the sport he played while at Harvard in the 1980s and Oxford in the 1990s. The decision to replace cricket is likely to be controversial among current and former staff, including former governor and cricket enthusiast Lord King, who participated in the match until his retirement last summer. David Buik, a veteran City commentator who has played at the Bank’s ground, described the decision to scrap cricket as outrageous. He said: ‘It is sacrilege. It is one of the most wonderful grounds you could ever wish to play on, and to deny the game because of exclusivity is awful. Cricket is one of our national games.’ The event usually features a match between 11 staff members and a governor’s team. Former England captain Andrew Strauss played in last year’s match, as did Chief Secretary to the Treasury Danny Alexander. Mr. Carney attended last year’s event, a day before assuming his role with an £874,000-a-year salary. Lord King, also a tennis fan and a regular at Wimbledon, is president of the Chance to Shine charity, which aims to increase participation in sports. The decision to ditch cricket is likely to raise eyebrows among staff past and present including former governor and keen cricketer Lord King, who took part in the match up to his retirement last summer. However, Mr. Carney is understood to have considered a match involving 22 men as too exclusive and wanted to include more women. He is a keen sportsman and was an ice hockey goalkeeper in his youth. He is a fan of Premier League side Everton and will no doubt be following Centre Court today, where fellow Canadian Eugenie Bouchard is competing at Wimbledon. The Bank denied that Mr. Carney ‘banned’ cricket and stated that staff were consulted about the events they would like to take place. A spokesman said: ‘The arrangements for the day were in the hands of staff. They chose a number of sports such as rounders, football, and tug-of-war among others.’
translated_content: Autor: Hugo Duncan. Bivši kanadski guverner Banke Engleske, Mark Carney, snimljen je s glavnim tajnikom državne riznice, Dannyjem Alexanderom, na jednom od prethodnih događaja. Za godišnju ljetnu zabavu Banke Engleske, guverner Mark Carney odlučio je da događaj treba biti inkluzivniji. Međutim, za mnoge zaposlenike, odluka kanadskog guvernera da promijeni tradiciju jednostavno 'nije bila fer'. Prvi strani guverner Banke organizirao je utakmicu roundersa umjesto kriketa jer vjeruje da je ljetna igra previše ekskluzivna. Ostale aktivnosti na događaju u Roehamptonu, jugozapadnom Londonu, koji se održava sutra, uključuju mali nogomet, tenis, utrku u troje, utrku s jajetom u žlici, potezanje užeta i bacanje čizme. Gospodin Carney nije išao toliko daleko da uvede hokej na ledu, sport koji je igrao dok je bio na Harvardu 1980-ih i Oxfordu 1990-ih. Odluka o zamjeni kriketa vjerojatno će biti kontroverzna među sadašnjim i bivšim zaposlenicima, uključujući bivšeg guvernera i ljubitelja kriketa lorda Kinga, koji je sudjelovao u utakmici do svog umirovljenja prošlog ljeta. David Buik, veteran gradski komentator koji je igrao na terenu Banke, opisao je odluku o ukidanju kriketa kao nečuvenu. Rekao je: 'To je svetogrđe. To je jedan od najljepših terena na kojem biste ikada poželjeli igrati, a uskratiti tu igru zbog ekskluzivnosti je užasno. Kriket je jedna od naših nacionalnih igara.' Događaj obično uključuje utakmicu između 11 zaposlenika i guvernerovog tima. Bivši kapetan Engleske Andrew Strauss igrao je u prošlogodišnjoj utakmici, kao i glavni tajnik državne riznice Danny Alexander. Gospodin Carney prisustvovao je prošlogodišnjem događaju, dan prije nego što je preuzeo svoju ulogu s godišnjom plaćom od 874.000 funti. Lord King, također ljubitelj tenisa i redovit posjetitelj Wimbledona, predsjednik je dobrotvorne organizacije Chance to Shine, koja ima za cilj povećati sudjelovanje u sportu. Odluka o ukidanju kriketa vjerojatno će izazvati iznenađenje među sadašnjim i bivšim zaposlenicima, uključujući bivšeg guvernera i strastvenog igrača kriketa lorda Kinga, koji je sudjelovao u utakmici do svog umirovljenja prošlog ljeta. Međutim, razumije se da je gospodin Carney smatrao utakmicu u kojoj sudjeluju 22 muškarca previše ekskluzivnom i želio je uključiti više žena. On je strastveni sportaš i bio je hokejski golman u mladosti. Navijač je momčadi Everton iz Premier lige i nesumnjivo će danas pratiti Centre Court, gdje se njegova kolegica Kanađanka Eugenie Bouchard natječe na Wimbledonu. Banka je demantirala da je gospodin Carney 'zabranio' kriket i izjavila da su se savjetovali sa zaposlenicima o događajima koje bi željeli da se održe. Glasnogovornik je rekao: 'Organizacija dana bila je u rukama zaposlenika. Odabrali su brojne sportove poput roundersa, nogometa i potezanja užeta, između ostalih.'
